A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLEM work, with matching architecture, experiments and figures. All supplied pages are readable, including v4 Appendices A–H. V1 ends with references and has no attached appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original quantum-operator prediction errors, band-structure comparisons, data-efficiency experiments and computational measurements in Tables I–IV and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V4 retains original solid-state experiments and adds molecular QH9 results for LEM in Appendix A and Table 6.

M1.justification: V4 Eqs. 15 and 17 specify alpha-weighted residual blending absent from v1's update equations, but v1 Figure 2 already depicts residual connections. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or completes its description. The core SLEM architecture is retained, and LEM was already named in v1's Code availability.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds static molecular QH9 evaluation using LEM, extending coverage beyond periodic materials to molecules with different structures and atom counts across training and testing. Conversely, the Si(600 K) scenario in v1 Table I disappears. MoS2, graphene, Si(300 K), GaN and HfO2 remain.

E2.justification: V4 adds QHnet as an evaluated comparator in Table 6. It removes HamGNN from the training-fraction comparison (v1 Table IV versus v4 Table 5) and training-time/memory comparison (Figure 5), while retaining HamGNN in the main Hamiltonian benchmark. These materially change comparator coverage across experiments.

E3.justification: The new QH9 experiment introduces a molecular OOD protocol with a stated 104,001/17,495/9,335 split, semilocal LEM evaluation, separate diagonal/off-diagonal Hamiltonian errors and density matrices inferred from predicted Hamiltonians. Separately, the reported HamGNN configuration changes from 10M to 2.8M parameters. Appendix E's settings for existing material datasets are additional disclosures, not established protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a focused OOD transferability test involving molecular structures and atom counts differing from training. The existing training-fraction sensitivity analysis retains its SLEM and DeepH-E3 results but loses HamGNN. No broader new ablation or robustness suite is supplied.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly supplies the MD velocity-initialization seed 449414 in its example LAMMPS input. This is limited seed disclosure; neither version reports repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests, and no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Retained SLEM and DeepH-E3 material scores largely match, but HamGNN MAEs change from 0.63/0.40/9.0 to 1.20/0.35/0.19 meV for MoS2/graphene/Si(300 K), alongside its changed model size. These are replaced results, not same-setting improvements. New QH9 results give LEM/QHnet overall Hamiltonian MAEs of 56.57/83.22 microhartree and density errors of 0.0219/0.0643; diagonal Hamiltonian errors instead favor QHnet, 155.24 versus 135.63. Si(600 K) and several HamGNN result entries are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a mathematical locality argument using atom-centered density decomposition and approximate cancellation of distant Hartree and external potentials under neutrality assumptions. V1 offered only brief screening motivation. This is a bounded heuristic derivation, not a new rigorous locality theorem; the existing SO(2) derivation is relocated to Appendix D.

C1.justification: The central claims remain localized equivariant prediction of multiple quantum operators, efficient high-order tensor products, inexpensive overlap prediction, data efficiency and potential large-system parallelization. V4's abstract newly mentions invariant overlap parameterization, but v1 already presents it as a contribution.

C2.justification: Appendices B, F and G substantially develop the locality rationale and its applicability boundaries. V4 distinguishes bond and environmental cutoffs, explains possible failure for molecular long-range dependencies, and motivates semilocal LEM when strict locality is unsuitable. V1 mainly supplies screening motivation and general future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds LAMMPS and ABACUS input examples, equilibration and sampling details, 150-training/30-testing frame counts, pseudopotential and functional choices, and an AISquare dataset link. Appendices F–G add cutoff-selection guidance and details of the previously named LEM variant. Existing DeePTB and dftio access information remains. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V4 adds QH9/QM9 references and sources for ABACUS, LAMMPS, pseudopotentials and the PBE functional. The main positioning relative to Allegro, equivariant message passing, SO(2) convolution and DeePTB remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodological explanations and results discussion undergo substantial condensation and rewriting. Discussion becomes Conclusion, while existing MPNN formalism, tensor-product details and future-work discussion move into Appendices C, D and H. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond adding new scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column ICLR layout. V1 Table I is split into v4 Tables 1–2, Table 6 is added, and Figures 4–5 change from vertically stacked to side-by-side panels. Figure 5 also removes HamGNN bars and revises its legend; the principal architecture and band-structure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reproducibility through concrete data-generation inputs and dataset access, and better explains when strict locality may fail. QH9 adds useful transfer evidence for LEM. These gains are tempered by removed Si(600 K) and HamGNN comparisons and new inconsistencies: Appendix A's 13,081 static structures conflict with its split totaling 130,831, while Appendix B gives screening lengths inconsistently in angstroms and atomic units. The net improvement is useful but limited.
